title: Variables
goal: In this lesson you will learn what a variable is and how to store a value so you can reuse it.
learn: A variable is a named box for a value
Print the variable name to show its value
idea: A variable is a named box that holds a value. You put something in the box with =, then use the name later instead of typing the value again. Text still needs quotes when you store it. Numbers do not need quotes.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change name = "Ava" to your own name (keep the quotes). Press Run. Both lines that use name should update.

practice.text: Store your name and age in variables. Use ONE print to show them in a sentence. Fill in the blank.
practice.hint: Do not retype "Sam" or 11 inside print. Use the variable names name and age so Python shows what is stored.
practice.starterTip: Try: print(name, "is", age, "years old"). Commas add spaces between the words and numbers.
practice.starter:
name = "Sam"
age = 11
# One print that uses both variables
print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if name and age are assigned to variables and a single print uses both variable names (not only hardcoded text for both).

practice.text: Create a variable for a favourite colour and print a sentence that uses it.
practice.hint: The colour variable is already set. Your print should include the word colour (the variable name), not only the word blue in quotes.
practice.starterTip: Example: print("My favourite colour is", colour). You can change the sentence, but keep colour in the print.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if a colour (or color) variable holds a non-empty string and print uses that variable name.

quiz.question: Which line correctly stores the text Maya in a variable called name?
quiz.correct: Text needs quotes, and the variable name goes on the left of =.
quiz.wrong: Put the variable name on the left, and put quotes around text values.

quiz.question: What is a variable?

options.text: A named box that holds a value
A blank line in the output

quiz.correct: A variable stores a value under a name you choose.
quiz.wrong: Think of a labeled box. The name lets you reuse the value.

quiz.question: Why use a variable instead of typing the same value many times?

options.text: Python requires every value to be in a variable
So you can reuse the value by its name

quiz.correct: Variables let you reuse a value without rewriting it everywhere.
quiz.wrong: The main reason is reuse. Not speed or a Python rule.
